A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same URSA work, retaining MMathCoT-1M, DualMath-1.1M and the foundation model. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite v5's substantial extension and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original URSA-8B benchmark results, verifier-guided inference experiments and data-synthesis ablations, including supplementary results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 reports original foundation-model and verifier results, plus PS-GRPO experiments, reward diagnostics, sensitivity tests and additional appendix studies.

M1.justification: v5 adds PS-GRPO, an online policy-optimization stage that penalizes outcome-correct rollouts when consecutive PRM scores exhibit a sufficiently large relative drop (Section 4; Algorithm 2). v3 ends with PRM training and test-time verification. The foundation architecture and principal data-synthesis engines are retained.

E1.justification: The six principal benchmark families and training-data sources remain. However, URSA's MathVista evaluation narrows from all five task categories in v3 Table 1 to GPS in v5, explicitly justified in Appendix F.3. v5 also introduces auxiliary diagram-captioning tests for encoder selection in Appendix D.

E2.justification: v5 adds evaluated comparators including Gemma3-12B, AtomThink-EMOVA and GPT-4o-mini. Its BoN comparisons add an InternVL2.5-8B outcome-reward baseline, while the new RL experiments compare PS-GRPO with vanilla GRPO and two scalar-process-reward variants. These substantially expand the comparison methods beyond v3.

E3.justification: v5 introduces an RL protocol using approximately 15.3K filtered prompts, eight rollouts per prompt and two training epochs, alongside new scaling and selection experiments. It also changes reported evaluation from rule-based matching to LLM judging for MathVista, MathVision and DYNAMATH (v3 Appendix B; v5 Appendix F.3). Existing alignment, SFT and PRM training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v5 adds analyses of scalar-reward failure, response shortening, drop-moment reliability, reward-parameter sensitivity and training-stage contributions. Appendices add SFT data-scaling, model-transfer, backbone-selection and synthesis-teacher comparisons. The original CoT-category ablation is retained in Appendix E.1 rather than being a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run variability, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Candidate-sampling counts and GRPO's reward normalization do not constitute new experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v5 adds PS-GRPO results, including 50.9 on MathVerse and 31.5 on MathVision, plus extensive transfer, scaling and BoN results. Retained URSA-8B scores also change: MathVista-GPS rises from 79.3 to 81.7 and MathVision from 26.2 to 28.7. Because judging procedures change, these updates do not establish gains under identical settings.

T1.justification: v5 adds mathematical definitions of the relative PRM-score drop and penalized outcome reward (Equations 5–6), together with GRPO and step-level advantage formulations in Appendix B.1. These provide limited additional formalization of the new procedure; the existing SFT/PRM losses remain, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v5 makes PRM-assisted online RL a central contribution and claims that PS-GRPO mitigates reward hacking and length bias while surpassing Gemma3-12B and GPT-4o in six-benchmark average performance. v3's core contributions concern synthesized reasoning data, the foundation model and PRM-guided test-time scaling, with RL left as future work.

C2.justification: v5 introduces explanations linking scalar process rewards to reward hacking and shorter reasoning, argues for relative reward drops as useful signals, and discusses penalty-related instability and false-positive rollouts (Sections 4 and 6.3; Appendix H). Conversely, v3's explicit qualification that MIE is distribution-specific is omitted.

D1.justification: v5 adds RL data-filtering instructions, PS-GRPO pseudocode, rollout and length limits, learning rate, KL coefficient, batch size and approximately 18-hour training cost. It also supplies an evaluation-judge prompt and additional data-construction details. The original alignment/SFT/PRM hyperparameter table is preserved as Table 13.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands positioning toward reinforcement learning and reward-design failures, adding references such as DeepSeek-R1, reward-hacking studies and multimodal RL methods. Appendix A also acknowledges concurrent visual-process-supervision work, including ViLBench, VisualPRM and MM-Verify, beyond v3's emphasis on data synthesis and inference-time verification.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around a new three-stage narrative. Related work moves to Appendix A, training stages become separate main sections, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded. Terminology also changes, including CoT distillation becoming CoT expansion and the verifier's naming.

P2.justification: v5 replaces the opening radar plot with grouped bars, redraws dataset statistics and the framework diagram, adds RL diagnostic plots, and consolidates headline results into a six-benchmark table. Existing tables and ablations are relocated or restructured, prompts and cases are redesigned, and the main text changes from two-column to single-column layout.

improvement.justification: v5 develops v3's prospective RL application into a specified method supported by matched GRPO controls, failure diagnostics, sensitivity tests and transfer experiments. Added scaling and design-selection studies also strengthen support for the retained framework. Narrower MathVista coverage and numerical inconsistencies, such as GPT-4o's GPS score being 62.6 in Figure 1 but 64.7 in Table 1, weaken comparative precision. Nevertheless, the gains in explanatory evidence and technical documentation constitute a substantial overall improvement.
